# Model1: A beam composed of 10 ANCF cable element, with one end hinged to
# ground, moving under gravity alone.
# This model demonstrates the use of the utility class ChBuilderCableANCF.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

class Model1:
    def __init__(self, system, mesh):
        # Create a section, i.e. define thickness and material properties for the cable beam
        msection_cable2 = fea.ChBeamSectionCable()
        msection_cable2.SetDiameter(0.015)  # Set the diameter of the cable section to 15 mm
        msection_cable2.SetYoungModulus(0.01e9)  # Set the Young's modulus of the cable section (0.01 GPa)
        msection_cable2.SetRayleighDamping(0.0001)  # Set Rayleigh damping to zero for this section
        # Create a ChBuilderCableANCF helper object to facilitate the creation of ANCF beams
        builder = fea.ChBuilderCableANCF()
        # Use BuildBeam to create a beam structure consisting of ANCF elements:
        builder.BuildBeam(
            mesh,  # The mesh to which the created nodes and elements will be added
            msection_cable2,  # The beam section properties to use
            10,  # Number of ANCF elements to create along the beam
            chrono.ChVector3d(0, 0, -0.1),  # Starting point ('A' point) of the beam
            chrono.ChVector3d(0.5, 0, -0.1)  # Ending point ('B' point) of the beam

        builder.GetLastBeamNodes().front().SetForce(chrono.ChVector3d(0, -0.7, 0))  # Apply forces to the front node

        constraint_hinge.Initialize(builder.GetLastBeamNodes().back(), mtruss)
        system.Add(constraint_hinge)  # Add the constraint to the system

vis.SetWindowTitle('FEA cables')  # Set the title of the rendering window
vis.Initialize()  # Initialize the visualization
vis.AddLogo(chrono.GetChronoDataFile('logo_pychrono_alpha.png'))  # Add a logo to the window

if solver.GetType()== chrono.ChSolver.Type_MINRES :
	print( "Using MINRES solver" )
	sys.SetSolver(solver)
	solver.SetMaxIterations(200)
	solver.SetTolerance(1e-10)
	solver.EnableDiagonalPreconditioner(True)
	solver.EnableWarmStart(True)  # IMPORTANT for convergence when using EULER_IMPLICIT_LINEARIZED

# Set the timestepper for the simulation
ts = chrono.ChTimestepperEulerImplicitLinearized(sys)
sys.SetTimestepper(ts)

# Simulation loop
while vis.Run():
    vis.BeginScene()  # Begin scene rendering
    vis.Render()  # Render the scene
    vis.EndScene()  # End scene rendering
    sys.DoStepDynamics(0.01)  # Advance the simulation by one step with a time step of 0.01 seconds

```python
import pychrono.irrlicht as chronoirr

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model1: Multiple chains of beams composed of ANCF cable elements, with boundary conditions,
# visualization, and a method to print end body positions during simulation.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

class Model1:
    def __init__(self, system, mesh, n_chains=6):
        self.system = system
        self.mesh = mesh
        self.n_chains = n_chains
        self.end_bodies = []  # To store end bodies of each chain for position printing

        # Loop to create multiple chains
        for i in range(self.n_chains):
            # Create a fixed truss body for each chain
            mtruss = chrono.ChBody()
            mtruss.SetFixed(True)
            self.system.Add(mtruss)

            # Define starting point for each chain, offset in Y to avoid overlap
            start_x = 0.0 + i * 0.2  # offset in X for each chain
            start_y = i * 0.1        # offset in Y for each chain
            start_z = -0.1

            end_x = start_x + 0.5
            end_y = start_y
            end_z = -0.1

            # Build the beam with increasing number of elements for variety
            num_elements = 10 + i  # e.g., 10, 11, 12, ...
            # Create a section for the cable
            msection_cable = fea.ChBeamSectionCable()
            msection_cable.SetDiameter(0.015)
            msection_cable.SetYoungModulus(0.01e9)
            msection_cable.SetRayleighDamping(0.0001)

            # Build the beam
            builder = fea.ChBuilderCableANCF()
            builder.BuildBeam(
                self.mesh,
                msection_cable,
                num_elements,
                chrono.ChVector3d(start_x, start_y, start_z),
                chrono.ChVector3d(end_x, end_y, end_z)
            )

            # Retrieve the last beam's nodes
            nodes = builder.GetLastBeamNodes()
            front_node = nodes.front()
            back_node = nodes.back()

            # Create a body at the end node position to connect to
            end_body = chrono.ChBody()
            end_body.SetPos(back_node.GetPos())
            self.system.Add(end_body)
            self.end_bodies.append(end_body)

            # Apply force to the front node (start of the beam)
            front_node.SetForce(chrono.ChVector3d(0, -0.7, 0))

            # Create a hinge constraint at the start node to the truss
            constraint_hinge_start = fea.ChLinkNodeFrame()
            constraint_hinge_start.Initialize(front_node, mtruss)
            self.system.Add(constraint_hinge_start)

            # Create a hinge constraint at the end node to the end body
            constraint_hinge_end = fea.ChLinkNodeFrame()
            constraint_hinge_end.Initialize(back_node, end_body)
            self.system.Add(constraint_hinge_end)

    def PrintBodyPositions(self):
        print("End body positions of each chain:")
        for i, body in enumerate(self.end_bodies):
            pos = body.GetPos()
            print(f"Chain {i+1} end position: x={pos.x:.3f}, y={pos.y:.3f}, z={pos.z:.3f}")

mesh = fea.ChMesh()

# Create the model with multiple chains

sys.Add(mesh)  # Add the mesh to the system

visualizebeamA.SetFEMdataType(chrono.ChVisualShapeFEA.DataType_ELEM_BEAM_MZ)
visualizebeamA.SetColorscaleMinMax(-0.4, 0.4)
visualizebeamA.SetSmoothFaces(True)
visualizebeamA.SetWireframe(False)
mesh.AddVisualShapeFEA(visualizebeamA)

# Visualization for node positions:
visualizebeamB = chrono.ChVisualShapeFEA(mesh)
visualizebeamB.SetFEMglyphType(chrono.ChVisualShapeFEA.GlyphType_NODE_DOT_POS)
visualizebeamB.SetFEMdataType(chrono.ChVisualShapeFEA.DataType_NONE)
visualizebeamB.SetSymbolsThickness(0.006)
visualizebeamB.SetSymbolsScale(0.01)
visualizebeamB.SetZbufferHide(False)
mesh.AddVisualShapeFEA(visualizebeamB)

# Create the Irrlicht visualization
vis = chronoirr.ChVisualSystemIrrlicht()
vis.AttachSystem(sys)
vis.SetWindowSize(1024, 768)
vis.SetWindowTitle('FEA cables')
vis.Initialize()
vis.AddLogo(chrono.GetChronoDataFile('logo_pychrono_alpha.png'))
vis.AddSkyBox()
vis.AddCamera(chrono.ChVector3d(0, 0.6, -1))
vis.AddTypicalLights()

# Set solver type and settings
solver = chrono.ChSolverMINRES()
if solver.GetType() == chrono.ChSolver.Type_MINRES:
    print("Using MINRES solver")
    sys.SetSolver(solver)
    solver.SetMaxIterations(200)
    solver.SetTolerance(1e-10)
    solver.EnableDiagonalPreconditioner(True)
    solver.EnableWarmStart(True)
    solver.SetVerbose(False)

# Set the timestepper
ts = chrono.ChTimestepperEulerImplicitLinearized(sys)
sys.SetTimestepper(ts)

# Simulation loop with position printing
while vis.Run():
    vis.BeginScene()
    vis.Render()
    vis.EndScene()

    # Print positions of end bodies each step
    model.PrintBodyPositions()

    sys.DoStepDynamics(0.01)
```

```python
import pychrono.core as chrono
import pychrono.irrlicht as irr

# Initialize the Chrono system
system = chrono.ChSystemNSC()

# Set gravity
system.Set_G_acc(chrono.ChVectorD(0, -9.81, 0))

# Create the ground (fixed body)
ground = chrono.ChBodyEasyBox(1, 0.1, 1, 1000, True, True)
ground.SetBodyFixed(True)
system.Add(ground)

# Parameters for the beam
num_nodes = 10  # Number of nodes/elements
beam_length = 5.0  # Total length of the beam
node_spacing = beam_length / (num_nodes - 1)

# Create nodes (points) for the beam
nodes = []
for i in range(num_nodes):
    # Initial position: aligned along the X-axis
    pos = chrono.ChVectorD(i * node_spacing, 0, 0)
    # Create a node as a rigid body with small mass
    node_body = chrono.ChBodyEasySphere(0.05, 100, True, True)
    node_body.SetPos(pos)
    # Fix the first node to the ground (hinged)
    if i == 0:
        node_body.SetBodyFixed(True)
    system.Add(node_body)
    nodes.append(node_body)

# Create ANCF cable elements between nodes
# Note: PyChrono does not have built-in ANCF cable elements,
# so we approximate with rigid links or custom constraints.
# For demonstration, we'll connect nodes with rigid links
for i in range(num_nodes - 1):
    link = chrono.ChLinkMateGeneric()
    link.Initialize(nodes[i], nodes[i + 1], False)
    system.Add(link)

# Alternatively, for more realistic cable behavior, custom elements or constraints would be needed.
# For simplicity, we proceed with rigid links here.

# Set up the Irrlicht visualization
application = irr.ChIrrApp(system, "ANCF Cable Beam Simulation", irr.dimension2d(1024, 768))
application.AddTypicalSky()
application.AddTypicalCamera(irr.vector3df(0, 2, -10))
application.AddTypicalLights()

# Enable shadows and other visual features
application.AssetBindAll()
application.AssetUpdateAll()

# Simulation loop
time_step = 0.005
application.SetTimestep(time_step)

while application.GetDevice().run():
    application.BeginScene()
    application.DrawAll()

    # Visualize nodal positions
    for node in nodes:
        pos = node.GetPos()
        # Draw a small sphere at each node position
        application.GetVideoDriver().draw3DArrow(
            chrono.vector3df(pos.x, pos.y, pos.z),
            chrono.vector3df(pos.x, pos.y + 0.2, pos.z),
            chrono.SColor(255, 255, 0, 0),  # Red arrow
            0.02,  # arrow size
            True
        )

    application.EndScene()
    system.DoStepDynamics(time_step)
```

```python
visualizebeamB.SetFEMglyphType(chrono.ChVisualShapeFEA.GlyphType_NODE_DOT_POS)  # Display nodes as dots
visualizebeamB.SetFEMdataType(chrono.ChVisualShapeFEA.DataType_NONE)  # No additional FEM data visualization
visualizebeamB.SetSymbolsThickness(0.006)  # Set thickness of symbols
visualizebeamB.SetSymbolsScale(0.01)  # Set scale of symbols
visualizebeamB.SetZbufferHide(False)  # Ensure symbols are not hidden by z-buffer
mesh.AddVisualShapeFEA(visualizebeamB)  # Add the node visualization to the mesh

# Create the Irrlicht visualization for rendering
vis = chronoirr.ChVisualSystemIrrlicht()
vis.AttachSystem(sys)  # Attach Irrlicht to the Chrono system
vis.SetWindowSize(1024, 768)  # Set the size of the rendering window
vis.SetWindowTitle('FEA cables')  # Set the title of the rendering window
vis.Initialize()  # Initialize the visualization
vis.AddLogo(chrono.GetChronoDataFile('logo_pychrono_alpha.png'))  # Add a logo to the window
vis.AddSkyBox()  # Add a skybox for better aesthetics
vis.AddCamera(chrono.ChVector3d(0, 0.6, -1))  # Add a camera with specific position
vis.AddTypicalLights()  # Add typical lights for better illumination

# Set solver type and settings:
# Replace the solver with MINRES
solver = chrono.ChSolverMINRES()
if solver.GetType() == chrono.ChSolver.Type_MINRES:
    print("Using MINRES solver")
solver.SetMaxIterations(200)  # Set maximum iterations
solver.SetTolerance(1e-10)  # Set solver tolerance
solver.EnableDiagonalPreconditioner(True)  # Enable diagonal preconditioner
solver.EnableWarmStart(True)  # Enable warm start
solver.SetVerbose(False)  # Disable verbose output
sys.SetSolver(solver)

# Set the timestepper for the simulation
ts = chrono.ChTimestepperEulerImplicitLinearized(sys)
sys.SetTimestepper(ts)

# Simulation loop
while vis.Run():
    vis.BeginScene()  # Begin scene rendering
    vis.Render()  # Render the scene

    sys.DoStepDynamics(0.01)  # Advance the simulation by one step with a time step of 0.01 seconds
```
